readerTitle: Why the world's biggest advertiser stopped showing you the same ad
caseNote: 실제 기업 (Procter & Gamble의 디지털 광고 조정) + 실제 연구 (Ehrenberg-Bass 연구소) + 가상 적용 (철물점 전단, 배관 업체 광고)
insight: 광고 예산은 '몇 번 보였나'가 아니라 '몇 명에게 닿았나'와 '한 사람이 몇 번 봤나'로 나눠 봐야 한다. 같은 노출 수도 도달이 넓을수록 새 고객을 더 만든다.
misconception: 노출 수가 같으면 효과도 같다. 이미 관심 있는 사람에게 여러 번 보여줄수록 광고가 더 잘 듣는다.

sources.text: The Wall Street Journal (2016년 8월). P&G가 정밀 타기팅 페이스북 광고 비중을 줄이기로 했다는 보도
Marc Pritchard(P&G 최고 브랜드 책임자)의 2017~2018년 공개 발언. 과도한 노출 빈도를 줄이고 디지털 광고비를 삭감했으며 도달은 늘었다는 내용
Sharp, B. (2010). How Brands Grow. Oxford University Press (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute 연구)
도달·빈도·총 노출(reach × frequency)의 표준 광고 개념

factChecks.note: P&G가 2016년 정밀 타기팅 페이스북 광고를 줄이겠다고 밝힌 WSJ 보도 날짜와 내용을 원문으로 확인하세요. 카드에는 '2016'과 '덜 의존하겠다'는 수준으로만 적었습니다.
Pritchard의 발언(디지털 광고비 삭감 규모, 도달 증가율)은 보도마다 수치가 다를 수 있어 카드에는 금액·비율을 넣지 않았습니다. 널리 인용되는 '약 2억 달러 삭감, 도달 10% 증가'를 쓰려면 1차 출처를 먼저 확인하세요.
Ehrenberg-Bass 주장(브랜드 구매자의 다수는 드물게 사는 가벼운 구매자이며, 성장은 주로 구매자 수 증가에서 온다)은 일반적 서술로만 적었습니다. 원문 표현을 확인하세요.

철물점 계산: 세 안 모두 전단 20,000장. A 5,000가구 × 4회 = 20,000, B 20,000가구 × 1회 = 20,000, C 10,000가구 × 2회 = 20,000. 배관 업체: 1,500명 × 평균 12회 = 월 18,000회 노출. 빈도를 3회로 줄이면 같은 노출로 최대 6,000명(18,000 ÷ 3)에게 닿을 수 있음(지역 인구가 충분하다는 가정). 모든 수치는 설명용.

cards.title: Why the world's biggest advertiser stopped showing you the same ad
body: Procter & Gamble spends more on advertising than almost any company on earth. It sells everyday goods like detergent, razors and toothpaste.
A few years ago it looked closely at who was seeing its online ads. Too often, it was the same people, again and again. Cutting those repeats became a way to spend less and reach more.

image.label: One person surrounded by many copies of the same ad
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 소파에 앉은 한 사람 주변에 똑같은 세제 광고 화면이 여러 개 떠 있고, 뒤편에는 광고를 하나도 못 본 사람들이 흐릿하게 서 있음. 실제 브랜드 로고나 제품 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: 20,000 flyers for a spring sale.
body: You run a hardware store. Your budget prints and mails 20,000 flyers for a spring garden sale. You have 5,000 regular customers. About 20,000 households live in your area, and most buy garden supplies only once or twice a year.

options.text: Four flyers each to your 5,000 regular customers
options.feedback: These people already know you, and many would come anyway. Each extra flyer adds less, and 15,000 nearby households hear nothing.

options.text: One flyer to each of the 20,000 households
options.feedback: You reach four times as many people, including occasional buyers who rarely think of you. Each household gets one reminder, which is the cost of this choice.

options.text: Two flyers each to the 10,000 closest homes
options.feedback: A reasonable middle ground that focuses on likely shoppers. But half your area never hears about the sale.

cards.title: P&G found it was talking to the same people.
body: In 2016, P&G said it would rely less on narrowly targeted Facebook ads. Aiming at small groups of likely buyers had shrunk its audience too much.

Later, chief brand officer Marc Pritchard described cutting online ad spending where the same people were seeing ads far too often. Spending went down. By P&G's account, the number of different people its ads reached went up.
The money wasn't the problem. Where it landed was.

cards.title: Reach and frequency
body: **Reach** is how many different people see your message at least once. **Frequency** is how many times, on average, each of them sees it.
Multiply the two and you get total impressions, the number most ad reports show first. But the same total can hide very different results: 20,000 people once, or 5,000 people four times.

image.label: Wide crowd with one dot each vs small group with many dots
image.brief: 좌우 비교 인포그래픽. 왼쪽 "Reach": 넓게 퍼진 많은 사람 아이콘에 점이 하나씩. 오른쪽 "Frequency": 소수의 사람 아이콘에 점이 여러 개씩. 가운데 "Same total impressions" 라벨.

cards.softwareNote: Ad dashboards often lead with impressions or clicks. Look for the reach and frequency columns too. A campaign showing a retargeting ad 15 times to past site visitors can look busy while reaching almost no one new.

cards.title: Same flyers, very different reach.
body: All three hardware store plans use 20,000 flyers. Only one reaches every household in the area.

cards.title: Most of your buyers barely think about you.
body: Researchers at the Ehrenberg-Bass Institute, summed up in Byron Sharp's book *How Brands Grow*, found a pattern across many categories. Most of a brand's buyers are **light buyers** who purchase rarely. Brands grow mainly by winning more buyers, not by getting loyal ones to buy more.
Light buyers are exactly the people a high-frequency plan misses. And each extra view to someone who has already seen your ad usually adds less than the last.

cards.title: Reach isn't everything.
body: Some repetition matters. People forget, and a new or complex message may need more than one view to stick. A reminder close to the moment of buying can also pay off.
Reach only counts if it reaches possible customers. A million views from people who can't buy from you is waste.
And ignore magic numbers like "people need to see an ad seven times." It's a popular rule of thumb, not a proven law. Test what your customers need.

cards.title: Now it's a plumbing business.
body: You run a plumbing company and spend $2,000 a month on local online ads. Most homeowners need a plumber only now and then, often urgently.
Your report says 1,500 people saw your ad, about 12 times each, in a month. What do you change?

image.label: Phone ad report showing reach 1,500 and frequency 12
image.brief: 스마트폰 화면의 광고 리포트. "Reach 1,500", "Frequency 12" 숫자가 크게 보이고, 화면 옆에 공구 가방을 든 배관공 캐릭터. 실제 광고 플랫폼 로고는 쓰지 않음.

options.text: Nothing. People who see it 12 times clearly can't miss you
options.feedback: Those 1,500 people surely remember you. But most homes in your area have never seen you, and many of them will need a plumber this year.

options.text: Cap frequency at about three a month and widen to your whole service area
options.feedback: The same budget could now reach far more households, so more people know your name when a pipe bursts. You give up some repetition, which is fine for a simple message.

options.text: Stop ads and rely on word of mouth
options.feedback: Referrals are valuable and free. But they grow slowly, and the problem wasn't the ads. It was who saw them.

cards.title: Count people before you count views.
body: Total impressions tell you how loud you were. Reach tells you how many people heard you. Spend first on reaching possible buyers, then add just enough repetition to be remembered.
**Try it today:** open your latest ad report or flyer plan. Write down how many different people it reached and how many times each saw it.
